analysis.title: JPM TECH SKETCH: Schilsky's Views on Tech Investing, GOOGL TPU Estimates Updated, AMZN Loses 40 Leos + SPCX Catches Starship, PANW Q1 Earnings Preview, TSLA Robotaxi Traction Building
key_insights: Schilsky says crowd-sourced petitions such as StandWithJensen.com cannot bring back NVDA's Jensen Huang because a corporate board is elected by shareholders. He sees a proxy fight to elect a new board, or an OpenAI-style employee revolt, as the only routes. He cites NY Times reporting that Huang violated the company's code of conduct through relationships with a customer and an employee.
Information Technology is 37% of the S&P 500 by market cap, near its highs. Schilsky says the average tech investor largely ignores macro factors such as rates, oil, wars, GDP and the Fed.

Multi-managers and quant funds are increasingly the marginal buyer of stocks on any given day and dominate Street equity trading revenue. Schilsky says this makes single-stock and thematic positioning extreme.

Hedge funds use AI heavily (some analysts' personal token budgets annualize to tens of thousands of dollars, a few above $100K), but Schilsky and the investors he speaks with are unsure it generates alpha for the average fundamental analyst.

Alt data from Yipit and M-Science no longer generates alpha, and some HF pods have dropped the subscriptions. Their estimates still become buyside quarterly expectations, for example the AWS revenue bogey is usually a simple average of Yipit and M-Science.
Twitter and podcasts now drive tech sentiment. Schilsky says fewer than 50 FinTwit influencers drive most of the debate, and public-company CEO podcast comments move stocks.

In tech, narrative beats value in the short term, earnings revisions matter more than price, and top-line growth of 20%+ or accelerating makes a stock 'ownable'. Whisper-number misses can still sink a stock when sell-side numbers are revised higher.
Positioning and sentiment drive the size of short-term moves, especially around earnings. Schilsky cites APP's Q3 earnings reaction as an example of extreme crowding.

In Internet, AI data-center capex has ended the capital-light model, raising volatility around capex guidance and capital raises. Investors still focus on GAAP EPS rather than FCF, so rising GAAP EPS keeps them long.

Internet sentiment is worse than Software for much of 2026. Generalists have moved from SMID Internet into Semis, leaving only specialists in names such as RDDT, APP, EBAY, ABNB and DUOL. Schilsky says generalists may return only if the Semis landscape looks 'a LOT worse'.

Disruption in Internet includes ChatGPT and AI Mode pressure on GOOGL Search, META Muse and AI agents pressuring online travel agencies (EXPE, BKNG) and e-commerce (AMZN, ETSY, W, EBAY), and AV technology threatening ride-share. AI ad tailwinds at META and GOOGL are crowding out PINS, SNAP and RDDT.

Alt research providers Cleveland and Edgewater took APP's stock down by about half from late summer into fall on channel checks that proved wrong. SemiAnalysis shaped buyside 2027 hyperscaler capex expectations.

In Software, only top-line acceleration is tolerated. SNOW, CRWD, NET and TEAM are seen as ownable on acceleration, while NOW, WDAY, INTU and MNDY are viewed as consensus shorts or underweights on deceleration.
Software valuation matters little. CRWD is up nearly 100% YTD and trades over 30x forward sales with mid-20s revenue growth, while Street FY28 revenue estimates are up only 4%.

Software sentiment is split. Infrastructure and Cybersecurity (DDOG, SNOW, PANW, CRWD, NET) are favored, and Applications (NOW, CRM, HUBS, ADBE, MNDY) are disfavored. IGV has bounced about one third off its February low and WCLD is up nearly 20% YTD.
Enterprise CISO channel checks after Mythos's release signalled a changed threat landscape and a buy case for Cybersecurity stocks.

In Media and Telecom, investors have used live entertainment (LYV, TKO, FWONA, SPHR, CNK) as an 'AI immune' and K-shaped economy trade. Schilsky expects this to continue while the stock market is rising.

SPCX is the disruptor in telecom. Starlink is a second disruption for cable broadband (CHTR, CMCSA) after wireless FWA, and Schilsky says a planned fourth wireless carrier would challenge VZ, T and TMUS.
NFLX and streaming peers struggle to grow subscribers as Instagram, YouTube and TikTok take watch time. Schilsky says NFLX is trying to become YouTube.

Schilsky uses SKYD as an example: guided 2030 FCF of $10B against a ~$40B market cap is about 4x, which he reads as the market not believing the estimate. Predecessor WBD missed similar far-out targets.

Schilsky expects media M&A to continue, citing NFLX's attempt to buy WBD (PSKY bought it instead), FOXA/ROKU, NXST/TGNA, CHTR/Cox, RKLB/IRDM, a possible FWONK sale, and the CMCSA split. Investors will not pay big multiples for synergy-driven EBITDA growth.

Ming-Chi Kuo estimates Google TPU shipments at 8-9M units in 2027, 14-15M in 2028 and 16-18M in 2029 given supply constraints. Shipments still grow in 2029 even though the market expects AI capex to peak in 2028. He calls MediaTek the biggest TPU winner as sole design supplier from v9 onward.
Similarweb says Reddit global visits fell 13% y/y from Oct 2025 to Oct 2026, with Google search referrals down. Reddit reports weekly active uniques up 16% y/y in October, a different measure.

A ULA Vulcan rocket failed shortly after launch on Sunday, destroying 40 Amazon Leo satellites in its first mission failure. SpaceX caught the Starship upper stage at its South Texas Mechazilla tower.
Zoox robotaxis are now on Uber in Las Vegas, the first third-party platform for Zoox, with Los Angeles planned for 2027.

JPM's Rajat says Tesla had about 1,306 registered robotaxi vehicles in Texas as of Nov 14 versus Waymo's 1,321. Cumulative unsupervised mileage is about 5.3M (vs ~1.4M at 3Q26 end), at a run-rate of about 635K miles per week. In Austin Tesla is estimated at ~50% of combined autonomous mileage, with a ~440 sq mi ODD vs Waymo's ~150. Cybercab customer sales launched this weekend.

JPM's Brian expects PANW to reiterate its FY27 NGS ARR outlook and sees potential upside to 1Q NGS ARR guidance of $9.54-9.56bn, driven by SASE, XSIAM and Idira. Guidance implies about $450mm net new NGS ARR, including close to $100mm from the final leg of a large AI-native customer migration onto Chronosphere. That contribution should normalize to $20-30mm in 2Q. Most post-Mythos benefit is expected in 2H given 6-9 month sales cycles.

market_movers.rationale: JPM sees potential upside to 1Q NGS ARR guidance of $9.54-9.56bn from SASE, XSIAM and Idira, and a favorable 2H setup from post-Mythos demand.
JPM sees early validation of Tesla's robotaxi fleet scaling, with Texas registered vehicles near Waymo's and rising unsupervised mileage.
Revenue growth accelerating keeps the stock ownable, despite trading over 30x forward sales.
Decelerating revenue growth leaves it viewed as a consensus short or underweight.
Decelerating growth leaves it viewed as a consensus short or underweight. JPM separately titles its Q127 preview 'Derisked Expectations'.
Subscriber growth is hard to come by as social video platforms take watch time.

sector_views.rationale: Sentiment is worse than Software, generalists have left SMID names, and AI disruption is spreading across Search, travel, e-commerce and ride-share.
Investors favor DDOG, SNOW, PANW, CRWD and NET on revenue acceleration and AI-driven threat demand.
AI coding agents threaten moats, and decelerating names such as NOW, WDAY, INTU and MNDY are consensus shorts.
LYV, TKO, FWONA, SPHR and CNK are an AI-immune trade benefiting from the K-shaped economy.
Starlink and a planned fourth wireless carrier from SPCX threaten CHTR, CMCSA, VZ, T and TMUS.

earnings_insights: PANW Q1 FY27 preview (JPM, estimate not yet reported): guidance for 1Q NGS ARR is $9.54-9.56bn, and JPM sees potential upside to it. Guidance implies about $450mm net new NGS ARR, including close to $100mm from the final leg of a migration onto Chronosphere, which PANW expects to normalize to $20-30mm in 2Q.
PANW: JPM expects the company to reiterate its FY27 NGS ARR outlook and to give more color on pipeline growth and deal conversions for a favorable 2H setup.
Schilsky cites APP's recent Q3 earnings reaction as an example of crowded positioning amplifying earnings moves. No figures given.
JPM preview titles in the headline list: INTU Q127 Preview 'Derisked Expectations' and ZM Q327 Earnings Preview 'Expect Beat-and-Raise'. No figures given in this document.
risk_factors: Schilsky says a Semis downturn could be the trigger for generalists to return to Internet.
Hyperscaler capex intensity is raising volatility around capex guidance and announced capital raises.
AI-driven software disruption could produce large volatility in Software, with much of the disruption not yet observed.
Cleveland and Edgewater channel checks cut APP's stock roughly in half before proving wrong, showing alt research risk.
Governance risk at NVDA, where the CEO's conduct has become a board-level issue.
Starlink and a fourth wireless carrier threaten cable and wireless incumbents.
vol_and_positioning: Schilsky says crowding in certain stocks and themes feels more extreme than ever, and multi-manager and quant dominance makes single-stock and thematic positioning extreme.
Schilsky says whisper-number misses can send a stock lower even when sell-side numbers are revised higher.
Generalists have rotated from Internet, especially SMID, into Semis, leaving specialists only in Internet names.

tension_points.bull_case: CRWD is up nearly 100% YTD on accelerating revenue and rising AI-driven threats, and infrastructure and cybersecurity names remain favored.
tension_points.bear_case: CRWD trades over 30x forward sales with mid-20s growth and Street FY28 revenue up only 4%, so the multiple rests on narrative rather than estimates.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Revenue growth decelerating, which Schilsky says turns a stock into a consensus short.

tension_points.bull_case: AI summarizes news and updates models, making analysts more efficient.
tension_points.bear_case: It is not clear that AI generates alpha for the average fundamental analyst because models lack true insight into markets.

theme_stances.key_argument: Investors have been bullish on infrastructure and cybersecurity names and bearish on applications software for the year, and Schilsky does not expect that to change soon.
AI coding agents could reverse-engineer software functionality cheaply, so investors question the moat of application software.
theme_stances.evidence: The cost of writing Software is headed towards zero.

theme_stances.key_argument: Starlink is a second disruption for cable broadband and a fourth wireless carrier would challenge incumbents.
theme_stances.evidence: SPCX is the true disruptor in the space – in telecom, specifically.
